review.title: Eggs for the Wrong Basket
review.headline: Two Farm rounds went wrong on confusion, then Casey's Hawk egg cracked round three.
review.summary: Round 1 and 2 ended with the table throwing at a confused Farm player whose odd egg count could not be explained. Meowfia won round 2 with a lone Sphinx who barely did anything. In round 3 a Hawk egg gave Casey certain proof, Blair was eggsecuted, and Farm banked big cards. Casey won with 20 points, mostly from one round of banking high cards.

rounds.recap: Blair was a confused Kookaburra with a stray +1 egg and a wrong Sphinx read. The whole table piled on Blair, who was Farm, so the two Meowfia (Alex, Drew) won while saying little. Many players threw Wilds and low cards.

Alex, a confused Kookaburra, got +2 eggs with no visible source. Everyone threw at Alex, a Farm player, even though Blair's Owl read said a Sphinx had visited Ellis. Lone Meowfia Finley won 6 points by throwing two 3s at the crowd.

Casey's Hawk egg proved Blair was Meowfia, and Alex's Owl read of a Floofer on Finley added support. Drew, the Floofer, tried to redirect, but the table threw at Blair anyway. Farm won and Casey, Ellis and Finley banked large cards.

highlights.text: Casey gained an egg from a Hawk visit on Blair and announced it as proof. Blair's cover collapsed within a beat.
Drew's Falcon read that Blair visited nobody shot down Blair's Hawk claim. It was Meowfia information used to hurt a Meowfia.
Finley, a lone Sphinx, claimed Falcon, was caught in a false visit and corrected it. Then Finley added two 3s to the mob on Alex and won.
Blair, a confused Farm Kookaburra, was convicted unanimously on an unexplained egg. The Meowfia just kept quiet and let it happen.

confusions.what: As Falcon, said Blair's +1 'looks like a Turkey'. Finley also repeated that Blair could not be Kookaburra, though confusion explained the odd report.
Said 'a Turkey can't visit anyone, so you can't be Kookaburra'. Blair never claimed Turkey, and Drew was Meowfia and knew Casey was Eagle.
Said Eagle Ellis should gain an egg from visiting Casey, but the Eagle only gains per visitor, and Casey had none.
Called Blair a probable Turkey and a liar although Blair's report said they were confused.
Argued a Turkey would gain from visitors, forgetting at first that a Floofer hug stops it. Finley corrected this later.
Claimed to have visited Drew, then changed it to Ellis. The Sphinx never visits a specific player by choice, and the lie was clumsy.
Mixed up the Kookaburra and Owl roles aloud, saying 'Blair-the-Kookaburra' and then correcting it.
Alex's Sphinx night action was filed as a wrong 'chooses' target, so the visit was lost. Players need a cleaner example of how the Sphinx picks.

worked: Hawk's egg gave Casey a certain, checkable proof of Meowfia in round 3. It created a real decision about whether to trust a lone claim.
Eagle, Falcon and Owl visit reports gave cross-checkable facts, such as Drew's Falcon read killing Blair's cover story.
Confused status produced believable noise, and honest Farm players had to admit that they could not explain their own count.
Throw sizes and the return of the best card made banking decisions interesting in round 3, when Casey's 7s and Ellis's 7 turned into big points.
problems: Confused made Farm players look guilty twice (Blair round 1, Alex round 2). Both were eggsecuted with no real evidence. Consider telling a confused player which stat is wrong, or making this less lethal.

Meowfia won two rounds by staying quiet while Farm convicted one of its own. Unexplained eggs act as an automatic scapegoat, so deduction is thin. Consider giving every round some solid checkable evidence.

Scores are hugely lopsided. Banking a few high cards in one winning round (Casey +14, Ellis +11) decided the game, so round 3 outweighed rounds 1 and 2. Consider capping banked values or scaling them.

Players invented claims that other facts quickly disproved, and the dialogue was repetitive. Most turns just restated 'who gave Alex the +2?' without new info. Consider fewer beats or a prompt that forces new information.
Role claims were often contradicted by the player's own mixed-up mechanics (Eagle, Turkey, Hawk). A short role cheat sheet might cut errors, and the Sphinx 'choose a role' action is awkward to read.
